ai.description: This caecilian reaches 15–20 cm in length. It is uniform dark violet-brown with a paler snout. Key features include a blunt, rounded head and 100–110 primary annuli encircling the body.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Gegeneophis carnosus* is distinguished by its unique lack of secondary grooves, resulting in a smooth body surface compared to the ringed appearance of other Indian species.
ai.habitat: *Gegeneophis carnosus* inhabits moist, leaf-litter-rich soil within evergreen tropical forests and plantations in the Western Ghats at elevations between 200 and 1,000 meters.
ai.behavior: The Periah Peak Caecilian is primarily nocturnal, emerging from its subterranean burrows to forage for earthworms and small invertebrates in moist soil after rainfall.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Gegeneophis carnosus* is oviparous, laying a small clutch of eggs in underground burrows during the pre-monsoon season (April–May) with maternal attendance.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Gegeneophis carnosus* is endemic to the southern Western Ghats in the Indian states of Kerala and Karnataka, typically found at elevations between 200 and 1,000 meters.
ai.callDescription: The Periah Peak Caecilian produces a high-pitched, repetitive "ticking" call, typically heard from within moist soil or leaf litter in its humid forest habitat.
